messages.text: Somerset title hopes suffer major blow in Yorkshire defeat as Notts also lose

metadata.summary: Somerset's hopes of becoming county champions for the first time in their history took a major blow as they collapsed to a costly defeat at the hands of Yorkshire.
metadata.content: County Championship: Somerset's title hopes hit badly in Yorkshire defeat as Notts also miss out to leave Warwickshire in command | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content County Championship: Somerset's title hopes hit badly in Yorkshire defeat as Notts also miss out to leave Warwickshire in command Somerset lose leadership of Division One to Warwickshire heading into the final round of matches after hugely-costly 185-run defeat to Yorkshire at Headingley; Somerset at home to Surrey, while Warwickshire host Leicestershire in final title-deciding matches from September 24 Friday 18 September 2026 14:39, UK Image: Yorkshire players congratulate Adam Lyth (l) for taking a catch from the bowling of Ben Coad to dismiss Somerset's James Rew (SWpix.com) Somerset's hopes of becoming county champions for the first time in their history took a major blow as they collapsed to a costly defeat at the hands of Yorkshire. Top of the County Championship Division One table heading into the penultimate round of matches, Somerset saw rivals Warwickshire wrap up a two-day victory against Essex but failed to keep pace at Headingley. Chasing 287 - the highest score of the match - they were bundled out for 101 on the final day. Resuming on 73-3 they collapsed horribly as their final seven wickets fell for 25 runs in less than 13 overs. metadata.content: Why Jurgen Klopp's 'one of 83 million' cap was significant as he named two Germany squads | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Why Jurgen Klopp's 'one of 83 million' cap was significant as he named two Germany squads Ahead of Germany's four matches against Netherlands, Serbia and Greece (two), Jurgen Klopp has called up 44 players in two different groups; "We need to rediscover the fun in all of this," said Klopp as he announced the squads By Sebastian Stafford-Bloor, The Athletic Friday 18 September 2026 12:58, UK Image: Jurgen Klopp has called up 44 players in two different groups ahead of Germany facing Netherlands, Serbia and Greece Jurgen Klopp has named two separate Germany squads for the upcoming Nations League matches in his first act as head coach. Ahead of the four matches against Netherlands, Serbia and Greece (two), Klopp has called up 44 players in two different groups. That list comprises 16 players who have yet to make an international appearance for Germany, including Said El Mala of Cologne, Max Rosenfelder, Philipp Treu and Derry Scherhant from Freiburg and Celtic midfielder Mika Baur. Other notable decisions include the omission of Stuttgart forward Deniz Undav, explained by Klopp as fitness-related, and his announcement that captain Joshua Kimmich will be used as a midfielder, having previously been utilised as a right-back by Julian Nagelsmann.
